newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN to airlift supplies to 100,000 Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN to airlift supplies to 100,000 Zaire refugees.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Thursday it would airlift emergency supplies for up to 100,000 Rwandan refugees located deep in east Zaire.

A UNHCR statement said food, blankets, plastic sheeting and medicine would be airlifted to Shabunda, 175 km (110 miles) west of eastern Zaire's Bukavu town, after a U.N. mission to the area this weekend.
"This is the first time we've located a significant number of refugees in the dense tropical forests of Zaire," U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata said in the statement.
"There are hundreds of thousands of refugees who remain unaccounted for and we need to reach them," she added.

The UNHCR said 10,000 refugees stricken with malnutrition and disease were in Shabunda and the International Committee of the Red Cross had located a further 90,000 scattered along the road further east.
An ethnic Tutsi rebellion in east Zaire in October uprooted 1.2 million Rwandan Hutu refugees who had fled their country in fear of reprisal for 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis.
Ogata said 560,000 Rwandan Hutus had returend home since mid-November but the rest were missing.

The United Nations, Western air forces and aid agencies have tried using satellite pictures and aerial surveys but failed to locate the refugees in the thick, inaccessible tropical rain forests of eastern Zaire.
Diplomats and aid officials say many of the refugees fear to return to Rwanda since they killed or watched others kill during the genocide.
